Word List
Every science word in this book, with a simple meaning you can read straight out to a six‑year‑old. Point at the word, read the meaning, then ask him to
say it back in his own words.
Living things
alive Something that grows, feeds, breathes and can make babies.
living thing Another way of saying something that is alive, like a person, an animal or a plant.
not alive Something that never grows or feeds, like a chair or a stone.
grow To get bigger over time.
breathe To take air in and let air out.
root The part of a plant under the soil. It drinks water and holds the plant down.
stem The part that holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
leaf The flat green part that catches sunlight to make the plant's food.
flower The colourful part where the plant makes its seeds.
seed The tiny thing a new plant grows out of.
healthy Strong and well, not sick.
senses The five ways we find out about the world: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
taste buds The tiny bumps on your tongue that tell you if food is sweet, salty or sour.
optometrist The eye doctor who checks that your eyes see clearly and gives you glasses.
Materials
object A thing, like a spoon or a cup.
material What the thing is made from, like wood, metal or plastic.
property What a material is like — hard, soft, shiny, bendy.
texture How something feels when you touch it: rough, smooth, bumpy or soft.
waterproof It does not let water through.
transparent You can see straight through it, like glass.
squash To press something so it becomes flatter.
stretch To pull something so it becomes longer.
potter A person who shapes clay to make pots and plates.
Forces, sound, electricity and magnets
force A push or a pull that makes something move or change shape.
push Moving something away from you.
pull Moving something towards you.
float To stay on top of the water.
sink To go down to the bottom of the water.
predict To say what you think will happen, before you try it.
source of sound Whatever the sound is coming from — a drum, a bell, your voice.
faint So quiet that it is hard to hear.
electricity The power that makes lamps, fridges and televisions work.
appliance A machine in the home that runs on electricity.
battery A small store of electricity you can carry, used in torches and clocks.
magnet A piece of metal that pulls iron and steel towards it.
attract To pull something towards you without touching it.
magnetic A material a magnet will pull, like iron or steel.
Earth and space
ocean The biggest water on Earth. It is salty.
lake A big area of still water with land all around it.
river Water that moves along the land, on its way to the sea.
stream A small, narrow river.
pond A small area of still water, where frogs like to live.
rock The hard, natural material the land is made from.
soil A mixture of tiny stones, sand, dead leaves and little creatures. Plants grow in it.
geologist A scientist who studies rocks and the ground.
planet A huge round world in space. We live on the planet Earth.
star A huge ball of burning gas that makes its own light. The Sun is a star.
astronaut A person who travels into space.
astronomer A scientist who studies the stars and space.
oxygen The part of the air that we need to breathe. There is none on the Moon.
Words a scientist uses
observe To look at something very carefully.
test To try something out to find the answer.
result What you found out at the end of a test.
sort To put things into groups that belong together.
measure To find out how big, how tall or how many.
chart A drawing that shows what you found out, so it is easy to read.
